dog.description_text:
This pet needs emergency placement. Please click here to go to our emergency placement page for more information.

This pet is available only through ACC New Hope partners. To adopt or foster, please complete the pre-screener form below. Inquiries sent directly to ACC will not receive a response.

Pre-Screener Form

Dior Chanel is at risk due to behavioral concerns. In Dior's original home, she was attacked by another dog. After being adopted, she displayed reactivity toward other animals and bit a larger dog that approached her. In the Care Centers, Dior has continued to show reactivity toward other dogs while on walks. She participates in training to help manage her arousal and is also working on muzzle training. Dior is social with staff and allows them to pet her. Medically, Dior has dental disease and a dermal mass.

Chanel Dior initially entered the Care Center in July 2026, and was returned by her adopter in September 2026. They describe her as a social, affectionate, independent, and playful dog. While in a home environment, Chanel Dior was reported to display on-leash reactivity towards other dogs, cats, and small animals, lunging and snapping. She has a history of a bite to another dog, which approached her quickly on leash. This was a bite and release, and the other dog did not require medical attention. Chanel Dior has also displayed mild resource guarding during her first stay at the care center, tensing and body blocking a toy. Due to the behavior shown in the home and care centers, we recommend that Chanel Dior be placed in an adult-only home through a New Hope partner, who can provide positive reinforcement-based, force-free behavior modification.

A volunteer writes: Dior Chanel has a special place in our heart right away. She is a 7 year old black beauty, with big ears and a white tipped chin. She had been with ACC over the summer and was even an event dog because of her social nature. I have so many videos of this cutie sleeping in her kennel - everything about her is perfection.
In her adoptive home, she had been "very affectionate, gentle" and done well with the children in the home. She had been very wiggly and outgoing with old friends and strangers. She was tolerant of baths and nail trims, house trained, and loves squeaky toys. They said she is "lovable, sweet, and affectionate" and is "a great addition to any home." She was returned from her adopter when the adopter did not feel comfortable helping her recover from kennel cough. She had lived with one of her puppies, but due to a dog biting her in the past, she is uncomfortable around novel dogs.
dog.name: Dior Chanel
